sets.q: Lesson 2 review. 927 ÷ 3 = ____
sets.why: 9 ÷ 3 → 3, 0 left. Bring down 2: 2 ÷ 3 → 0 (write the 0!), 2 left. Bring down 7: 27 ÷ 3 → 9, 0 left. 309. Check: 3 × 309 = 927.
sets.no: When 3 doesn't go into a digit, write a 0 in the quotient and bring down the next digit.

sets.q: Which decimal is the GREATEST?
sets.why: Write them all with 3 decimal places: 0.465, 0.050, 0.500, 0.470. 0.5 (0.500) is the greatest.
no: More digits does not mean bigger: 0.465 is less than 0.500.

sets.q: What text structure does this source use?

visual.text:
Practice source
The Foggy Morning
“On Tuesday, thick fog covered the town of Cedar Bend. Because drivers could see only a few feet ahead, the school buses crept along and arrived 40 minutes late. As a result, first period started late, so Mr. Ortiz moved the spelling test to the afternoon. By 10am the sun had burned the fog away.”

sets.why: Because, as a result and so show what the fog made happen. That is cause and effect.
no: It mentions times, but it does not give steps to follow. It shows what the fog caused.
It does not show how two things are alike and different.
Nobody fixes anything. The fog just leads to one effect after another.

sets.q: How many minutes late did the buses arrive? Type the number.

sets.q: What text structure does this source use?

visual.text:
Practice source
The Muddy Path
“After every rainstorm, students at Oak Grove School tracked mud down the hallways. The path from the bus stop to the front door was bare dirt. To fix this, the student council asked the principal for help. Together, they set 60 flat stepping stones along the path. Now shoes stay clean, and the custodian spends less time mopping.”

sets.why: The mud is the problem. “To fix this” is a signal: the stepping stones are the solution. That is problem and solution.
no: It does not give steps in time order. It names a problem and tells how it was fixed.
It does not show how two things are alike and different.
Mud does cause messy halls, but the whole piece is built around fixing that problem.

sets.q: How many stepping stones did they set along the path? Type the number.
